steps.title: Weigh and label samples
steps.instruction: Weigh 500 mg of each material (spinach, red cabbage, Roma tomato, carrots, coffee, green‑tea bag, lemon‑tea bag, spirulina flakes) into separate vials and label the vials 1–8 accordingly.

steps.title: Add ethanol and dissolve
steps.instruction: Using a pipettor with a tip, add 1 mL ethanol to each vial. After ~2 minutes the fish‑flake vial will have absorbed the solvent; add an additional 2 mL ethanol to that vial (total 3 mL). Vortex all vials to mix, then let the solutions sit for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare TLC chambers
steps.instruction: Using a graduated cylinder, prepare two TLC chambers. For chamber 1, mix 50 mL ethyl acetate with 50 mL cyclohexane (1:1 v/v) to a total of 100 mL and place the mixture in beaker 1. For chamber 2, mix 25 mL ethyl acetate with 75 mL cyclohexane (1:4 v/v) to a total of 100 mL and place the mixture in beaker 2. Cover each beaker with aluminum foil.

steps.title: Label plates and draw baseline
steps.instruction: On each of two TLC plates, draw a pencil baseline above the future solvent level and mark eight lanes numbered 1–8 that correspond to the vials.

steps.title: Spot samples onto plates
steps.instruction: Using a spotting pipette, apply the solution from each vial onto the matching lane of both plates. After each spot, dip the pipette into a vial of ethanol and dry it on a paper towel before the next spot. Allow each spot to dry before proceeding. Spot in the order: red cabbage (lane 1), spinach (lane 2), then the remaining samples in the same order as weighed in Step 1.

steps.title: Develop plates in chambers
steps.instruction: Place TLC plate 1 into chamber 1 and ensure the baseline remains above the solvent level; place aluminum foil on top of the beaker and let the solvent rise. Likewise, place TLC plate 2 into chamber 2 with the baseline above the solvent level and cover with foil. Allow development until the solvent front approaches the top of the plate but does not exceed the plate length.

steps.title: Visualize plates and record
steps.instruction: When the solvent front is near the top (≈5–10 minutes), remove each plate, immediately mark the solvent front, photograph the plate, then stain with CAM stain. Measure the distance from baseline to the centre of each spot (X) and from baseline to the solvent front (Y); calculate Rf = X/Y for each spot.
